product.description: Python APIs for EduceLab imaging hardware (cameras, lights, stages, USB hubs); the basis for all hardware-interfacing projects in the lab
product.problem: Device code is duplicated per project and coupled to each project's framework (Qt in pgs-scan, tkinter threads in the spectral prototype); copies drift, carry their own bugs (#71, #83, #84, #90), and hardware knowledge is scattered or lost
product.target_users: Primary: lab developers building acquisition applications (pgs-scan now, future rigs). Secondary: rig operators running el-devices hardware checks
key_goals: One blocking, framework-free API per hardware type that any consumer can wrap
Port spectral devices first (MISHA, Foldio360, gphoto2 + focus), then pgs-scan dev devices (XLC, X-Carve, Spinnaker), then the Acroname hub
Simulated devices and a shared contract test suite for hardware-free development
Hardware reference docs capturing everything known, published with API docs on GitHub Pages
pgs-scan migrated as the first full consumer
product.source: inferred from the 2026-10-12 design session (CONTEXT.md, docs/adr/); confirmed by maintainer

guidelines.voice_and_tone: Precise, technical, evidence-first; explicit about uncertainty (verified/assumed/unknown)
design_principles: Report what the hardware did, not what we wished (ADR 0002, ADR 0003)
Write down what the hardware actually does
guidelines.source: inferred from design session and flex-recon conventions; confirmed by maintainer

languages: Python >=3.11 (CI: 3.11-3.14 on ubuntu/macos/windows); Spinnaker driver 3.12 only
tech_stack.packaging: setuptools, PEP 621 pyproject.toml, educelab namespace package; pip and uv both supported, nothing may require uv
tech_stack.database: none; library persists nothing (CameraFile.save() is the only writer)

optional_extras.spinnaker: PySpin not on PyPI; manual install from Spinnaker SDK, no extra

tech_stack.dev_tooling: pytest (hardware marker), ruff check + format, pytest-cov (reported, no threshold), mypy (advisory)
tech_stack.docs_tooling: MkDocs Material + mkdocstrings in a docs dependency group
tech_stack.infrastructure: GitHub Actions CI (pip), docs deployed to GitHub Pages; consumers install from git tags, 0.x semver, PyPI later
tech_stack.source: detected from pyproject.toml and .github/workflows/tests.yml plus design session; confirmed by maintainer

workflow.tdd_strictness: moderate; fake-transport protocol tests and shared contract tests (real + simulated) required for every driver; hardware-marked tests written but non-blocking
workflow.commit_strategy: descriptive imperative subjects, no Conventional Commits prefix
workflow.code_review: at most one PR per track (squash-merged to main); never a PR per task or phase; small doc/glossary fixes commit directly to main. Maintainer dislikes PR-heavy workflows
workflow.verification_checkpoints: after each phase; maintainer approval for role ABC signature, CONTEXT.md glossary, and ADR changes; driver tracks end with a manual el-devices hardware check
workflow.source: adapted from flex-recon/pgs-scan defaults; confirmed by maintainer

styleguides.existing_configs_incorporated: pyproject.toml [tool.ruff] (src) and [tool.ruff.lint] extend-select I, UP, B; ruff defaults otherwise. Adapted from flex-recon's guides, condensed, plus user CLAUDE.md comment/docstring rules
